question: Adopt a standing rule that overnight runs do all git work from a dedicated side-copy (worktree), never the main checkout? Raised by conflict log §1: a concurrent attended session switched the main checkout mid-card and the run's first W0 merge landed on dev (recovered in full).
proposal: Yes — record as a candidate rule the operator approves before it binds (chosen over writing it into CLAUDE.md immediately, and over leaving it a one-off incident note)

votes.note: protects the operator's own attended work from run collisions; consent-gated adoption matches how every other standing rule entered force
the hazard class was already flagged at slate sign-off (signed on stale premises); this is the second occurrence and it moved a git write — a standing rule is proportionate
the run already proved the mechanism works — all post-incident git ops ran from hq-worktrees/run-20260807 without further collision; zero new machinery needed

cited.statement: Test suites run against their own Postgres container, never the cluster serving production. A test mistake must be structurally unable to touch operating data — no test file holds admin credentials to production.
cited.fit: same structural-isolation principle: a mistake must be structurally unable to touch the shared thing — P-1 applies it to test databases vs production; this applies it to run git-ops vs the attended checkout

weighing: Only operations/P-1 bears, and it points the same direction as all three votes; the question still went to the operator because adopting a standing rule is policy-setting, not a preference application — escalation was the correct disposition.
